Works with

Rugged tablet for Limble CMMS

Limble is a cloud-based CMMS used by maintenance, facilities and engineering teams in manufacturing, food and beverage, energy, healthcare, hospitality, property and fleet. Managers plan preventive maintenance and run reports in a desktop browser. Technicians carry the Limble mobile app on a phone or tablet to open work orders, follow task instructions, scan asset QR codes, log time, consume parts and add completion notes, often on a plant floor, a roof or a remote site.

A consumer tablet does not last long in that environment. It is not sealed against dust and wash-down water, its glass cracks when it drops from a ladder, the screen washes out under skylights, and the battery runs flat before the end of a shift. When a plant has poor Wi-Fi, a device without 4G leaves the technician waiting to sync.

This page lists what Limble publishes about the devices it runs on, matches those requirements to the four Tuga rugged devices we sell in the UK, and explains the limits honestly, including the parts of Limble that only work on certain plans.

Requirements

What Limble CMMS needs from a device

Each item below comes from Limble Solutions, Inc.'s own listing or documentation, with the source linked.

  • Android 7.0 or later for the Limble mobile app

    The Google Play listing for the new Limble app (package com.limblecmms.mobileApp, developer Limble Solutions, version 2.0.4, updated 28 September 2026) states that it requires Android 7.0 and up. The older Limble CMMS (Legacy) app (version 3.2.3, updated 28 July 2025) requires Android 6.0 and up, and its listing says it will remain available during the transition to the new app. Source: play.google.com

  • Vendor device recommendations: 4GB RAM, 2GHz quad-core processor, a camera, a recent Android version

    Limble's Mobile Device Best Practices article describes these as recommendations for best results and not requirements: at least 2GB RAM with 4GB recommended, a processor with at least 2GHz top speed and at least 4 physical cores, any camera as long as the device has one, the latest two versions of Android or iOS, and a device under four years old. No make or model is named and no screen size guidance is published. Source: help.limblecmms.com

  • Camera for QR code scanning

    Limble's barcode article says that from the mobile app you click Scan QR Code, and when the camera appears you scan the barcode and the matching part or asset card opens. Imported non-Limble barcodes are read the same way, although Limble's new app article lists non-Limble barcodes as not yet available in the new app. No dedicated or Bluetooth scanner is mentioned in Limble's documentation. Source: help.limblecmms.com

  • Offline mode: Premium+ and Enterprise plans, mobile app only, limited scope

    Mobile App Offline Mode is listed under Premium+ and Enterprise on Limble's pricing page, not Standard. In the new app, offline work covers bookmarked tasks that are fully downloaded (completing instructions, logging time, consuming already-associated parts, adding completion notes) plus QR code scanning. You cannot create tasks, add parts to tasks, request purchases or edit asset or part data offline, and Limble warns not to close the app while working offline or in-progress work may be lost. Source: help.limblecmms.com

  • Windows: a supported desktop browser, no native Windows app

    Limble's help centre lists supported browsers as Chrome (latest major version), Microsoft Edge (latest two major versions), Firefox (latest major version or ESR) and Safari (latest two major versions). Internet Explorer and the legacy version of Edge are not supported. Limble recommends at least 30 Mbps download and 2 Mbps upload. We found no Windows app or Microsoft Store listing; Windows users run the web app in a browser. Source: help.limblecmms.com

  • Connectivity for syncing work orders

    Limble is cloud-based and the mobile app works online or offline, but offline access depends on plan and on tasks being downloaded first. The legacy app's offline article states you must first be logged into Limble and sync your task data before entering offline mode, so a device with its own mobile data connection reduces the chance of a technician reaching a site without their tasks. Source: help.limblecmms.com

Limble has no native Windows app, but managers and supervisors who configure PMs, build dashboards and run reports do that in a desktop browser. The Tuga W10 runs Windows 11 Pro, so it can run Edge or Chrome, both on Limble's supported browser list, and therefore the full Limble web app on the shop floor. It suits a site that standardises on Windows, needs Ethernet for a fixed workstation, or wants to put Limble dashboards on a screen over HDMI. It is not the right device for Limble's mobile offline mode, which is an Android and iOS app feature, and its IP65 rating covers water jets but not immersion.

Worth knowing. Limble's offline mode is only included in the Premium+ and Enterprise plans, and even then it covers bookmarked, fully downloaded tasks in the mobile app rather than everything. No tablet changes that. There is no native Windows app, so the Tuga W10 runs Limble in a browser and does not get the mobile offline mode. Limble does not document NFC or RFID support, so although the A10, A8, A6 and W10 have NFC hardware, we make no claim that Limble uses it. The new Limble app launched with English-language support and Limble's help article now lists multi-language support; the same article lists non-Limble barcodes, purchasing, vendors and some custom dashboards as not yet available in the new app, with the legacy app remaining available during the transition. Limble's own device article says many customers have had success with recent Apple phones and tablets; it does not recommend any Android make or model, and we do not claim the Tuga devices are tested or approved by Limble.
Setting up

Getting Limble CMMS running

  1. Use your existing Limble account, or have your Limble administrator create user logins for each technician.
  2. On a Tuga A10, A8 or A6, open Google Play and install the Limble app (developer Limble Solutions). If your team still uses the older app, it is listed separately as Limble CMMS (Legacy). On a Tuga W10, open Edge or Chrome and go to your Limble web address.
  3. Sign in with the technician's Limble credentials. Allow camera access if prompted so the Scan QR Code function can read asset labels.
  4. If your plan is Premium+ or Enterprise and you need offline mode, follow Limble's help article for your app version. In the new app, bookmark the tasks you need so they download before you lose signal. In the legacy app, offline mode is off by default and is enabled per user under Edit Profile, and task data must be synced before going offline.
  5. Print and attach Limble QR codes to assets, then test a scan on the device before rolling out to the whole team.
  6. On the A10, fit the hand strap from the box. Add a screen protector, and install a charging dock or vehicle mounting dock where devices are stored or carried between jobs.
